text:
maya: :rotating_light: seeing a sudden provisioning surge in us-west1. GPU pool allocs are failing, queue depth spiked to 80% and avg wait ~65s. Notified infra alerts at 08:12 UTC.

ops-bot: Alert: gpu-provisioner-us-west1 - 5xx rate from hypervisor API, 08:12:34 UTC.

jonathan: I'm on it. Can folks paste the latest scheduler logs? wondering if autoscaler is failing or if it's host-level OOMs.

paul_s: grabbing logs now. quick snippet:
```
E0802 08:12:18.123 scheduler.go:214] failed to provision instance: insufficient resources: gpu:0 -> allocation rejected
W0802 08:12:19.457 worker.go:88] hypervisor returned 502 on /allocate (driver timeout)
E0802 08:12:22.009 eviction_manager.go:76] host cg-mil-23: kernel OOM-killer invoked, killing process "inferd"
```

paul_s: looks like host-level evictions plus intermittent API 502s to the hypervisor. We've got a partial pool blackout rather than a full region network outage.

jonathan: good context. Immediate plan: 1) failover routing for non-critical traffic to us-east1 and eu-west1, 2) reserve remaining us-west capacity for SLA-tagged customers, 3) spike up preemptible pools in us-east to absorb short-term requests. Thoughts on cost/latency tradeoffs?

irene_cs: need to flag our top 10 impacted customers now. CSMs should send one-line heads up. If we route to eu-west1, embeddings and chat latency may increase for NA customers — call that out.

csm-ella: I can message the ten. Prefer we have a status page blurb before outreach. Sales hates surprises.

maya: Agreed. Draft for status page (suggested):
"Investigating increased provisioning failures in our US-West GPU pool. Some customers may experience degraded throughput and longer queuing times. We are shifting lower-priority traffic to other regions and reserving remaining US-West capacity for service-tier customers. We will provide updates and an ETA within 90 minutes"

irene_cs: change "lower-priority" to "non-SLA" and add note about potential cross-region egress charges for customers with egress enabled.

maya: updated draft: 
"Investigating increased provisioning failures in our US-West GPU pool. Some customers may experience degraded throughput and queueing. We are shifting non-SLA traffic to other regions and reserving remaining US-West capacity for SLA customers. Traffic reroutes may incur additional cross-region egress charges; we will surface impacted billing lines. ETA 90 minutes for next update."

jonathan: +1. Add a short internal blurb for support:
```
Impact: Provisioning failures in us-west1 causing increased latency and failed requests for non-SLA workloads.
Mitigation: Traffic reroutes to us-east1/eu-west1, preemptible pool spin-up, reserve remaining us-west capacity for SLA customers.
ETA: 90 minutes (monitoring and scaling attempts ongoing).
Contact: irene_cs / srep-oncall for customer escalations.
```

paul_s: technical note — if we route >30% traffic off-region we'll see egress cost delta ~+0.8c/token on high-throughput workloads (estimate). Also watch for model cold-start latency on cross-region KV caches.

jonathan: thanks Paul. For the reroute we can run this control-plane command (testing in staging now):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood.ai/v1/routing/override \
  -d '{"from":"us-west1","to":["us-east1","eu-west1"],"selector":"tier!=SLA","percent":60}'
```

maya: who wants to own the status page publish and support pin?

irene_cs: I'll publish the status page with the updated text and post the internal blurb to #support. csm-ella will send the VIP notes.

csm-ella: sending messages to customers now — will CC ops thread for any replies.

srep-oncall: I'm standing by for escalations. If we need to temporarily bump priority for an account, we should use the emergency capacity routing and bill the delta. Confirmed we have a manual override playbook.

jonathan: okay executing incremental plan: 1) spin preemptible pool in us-east1 (30 instances), 2) run routing override at 15:02 UTC to shift 60% non-SLA traffic, 3) cordon problematic hosts in us-west1 and scale replacement nodes.

paul_s: done: preemptible pool request created (request id: prq-7f3b). cordoned hosts: cg-mil-23, cg-mil-24.

ops-bot: Action: routing override applied (audit id rtv-22a), timestamp 08:18:44 UTC.

maya: posting status page now. Internal note: avoid posting dollar estimates publicly. Discuss billing impacts via CS follow-up.

irene_cs: status page posted. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2187654321 - please use that for external updates.

csm-ella: customer batch 1 sent, awaiting replies. Two customers asked for ETA on SLA fallback — directing them to srep-oncall.

jonathan: monitoring queues — initial improvement: avg wait down from 65s -> 28s after routing. Still seeing some 502s from older hypervisors; root cause likely kernel OOM under memory pressure.

paul_s: long-term follow-up items: root-cause postmortem, increase host swap thresholds, review eviction policy, and evaluate replacing older hypervisor pool over next 48h.

maya: thanks team. Next update in 45 minutes or sooner if status changes. :thumbsup:
